“Be a philosopher; but, amidst all your philosophy, be still a man.” — David Hume (Q0394)

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with A Treatise of Human Nature I.4.7, within the Scottish Enlightenment tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of philosophy, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In David Hume's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
